model.name: ML Model Artifact
model.purpose: Govern a versioned machine-learning model artifact as a distinct, inspectable object: identity, payload, interface, composition, documentation, attached evidence, rights, risk metadata, and registry lifecycle, so an agent can create, retrieve, validate, promote, interchange, and retire the artifact without absorbing the AI system, training-run, or evaluation-campaign models.
model.scope_statement: This model covers one trained or otherwise parameterized machine-learning model artifact and the metadata required to identify, reconstruct, license, evaluate-as-subject, interchange, and operate that artifact. It is format-neutral: ONNX graphs, Safetensors shards, registry URIs, SPDX packages, and CycloneDX components are projections of the same entity. Training processes, evaluation campaigns, datasets, and the AI system that consumes the artifact are referenced, not owned.
in_scope: Canonical and global identifiers, versions, revisions, and successor links for a model artifact
Task, modality, library, architecture family, learning approach, and foundation or general-purpose classification
Serializable payload members (weights, tensors, graphs, configs) and cryptographic integrity
Input and output contract, parameter scale, and interchange graph metadata
Derivation relations (base model, fine-tune, adapter, quantization, merge) as references
Lineage pointers to the producing training run, datasets, and hyperparameters attached to the artifact
Model-card intended use, limitations, licence, acceptable use, and attached quantitative results
GPAI technical-documentation and downstream-information packs where the artifact is a general-purpose AI model
Registry stages, aliases, ownership, access, retention, and deletion of the artifact record and payload
out_of_scope: The enclosing AI system, product, or agent runtime (WM-AI-001)
The training, fine-tuning, or experiment run that produced the artifact (WM-AI-006)
The evaluation campaign or test harness as a process (WM-AI-003); only results attached to this artifact are in scope
Datasets, data cards, and data-governance objects except as references
Inference endpoints, gateways, prompts, tools, RAG indexes, and serving configuration
People, organizations, and hardware assets as first-class entities
Framework libraries and OS packages except as ML-BOM dependency references

boundary_notes.distinction: An AI system uses one or more model artifacts; the system includes orchestration, data paths, and human oversight. This model stops at the versioned model object that the system loads.

A training or fine-tuning run produces the artifact and holds experiment parameters, code, and metrics of the job. This model stores only lineage references and the hyperparameters copied onto the resulting artifact.
Evaluation assesses a model artifact and owns protocols, splits, and campaign state. This model stores attached metrics, thresholds, and evidence pointers, not the evaluation process.
Training, validation, and test datasets are separate governed objects. The artifact records identifiers and provenance pointers, not dataset contents or data-quality processes.
Runtime and training libraries are software components. An ML model is a distinct component type (CycloneDX machine-learning-model; SPDX AIPackage) that may appear beside, not as, those libraries.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), NIST AI 100-1
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Separates the AI model dimension from the AI system; requires documented inventory, intended use and knowledge limits, mapped components, and model explanation, validation, and documentation (MAP/MEASURE/GOVERN).

sources.title: Hugging Face Hub documentation: Model Cards
sources.relevance: Defines the de facto public model-artifact card: identity metadata, licence, datasets, base-model derivation, pipeline task, library, evaluation results, and human-readable intended use and limitations.

sources.title: CycloneDX v1.6 JSON Reference (ECMA-424, 1st Edition)
sources.relevance: Normative component type machine-learning-model, hashes, PURL, licences, supplier/manufacturer, and modelCard (parameters, quantitative analysis, considerations, environmental data) for ML-BOM inventory.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1: AIPackage class
sources.relevance: Canonical AI package/model artifact properties: spdxId, name, packageVersion, downloadLocation, suppliedBy, releaseTime, verifiedUsing, typeOfModel, hyperparameters, metrics, limitations, energy, sensitive-personal-information, safety risk, validUntilTime.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 Information technology — Artificial intelligence — Artificial intelligence concepts and terminology
sources.relevance: Terminology baseline for AI model, machine-learning model, and (in AMD1 draft) foundation model and large language model, distinguishing a model from an AI system.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 23053:2022 Framework for Artificial Intelligence (AI) Systems Using Machine Learning (ML)
sources.relevance: Places the trained model inside the ML-system framework and pipeline (data, modelling, verification and validation, deployment, operation) so the artifact is a component, not the whole system.

sources.title: MLflow Model Registry documentation
sources.relevance: Operational registry semantics: registered model, immutable version, URI, aliases, tags, lineage to producing run, signatures, and promotion workflows.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Article 53 — Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
sources.version_or_date: OJ L 2024/1689, 13 June 2024; Art. 53 applicable 2 August 2025
sources.relevance: Legal duties on a GPAI model artifact: keep Annex XI technical documentation, supply Annex XII packs to downstream system providers, copyright policy, public training-content summary, and limited open-source exemption when weights, architecture, and usage information are public.

sources.title: Hugging Face Hub modelcard.md metadata specification
sources.relevance: Machine-validated YAML schema for licence, library_name, datasets, base_model, metrics, and model-index evaluation results including source URL and optional verifyToken.

sources.title: Introduction to ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) 1.23.0
sources.relevance: Interchange graph semantics for a model artifact: inputs, outputs, nodes, initializers (weights), opset, protobuf serialization, metadata, and shape/type inference.

sources.title: Safetensors documentation
sources.relevance: Widely used tensor-payload format for weight artifacts, designed as a safer alternative to pickle serialization.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1: AI profile namespace
sources.relevance: States that the AI namespace documents AI system and model artifacts as tangible outputs of development (packages, models, datasets) and requires declared and concluded licence relationships on every AIPackage.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Annex XI — Technical documentation for providers of general-purpose AI models
sources.relevance: Minimum technical-documentation content for a GPAI model: tasks, AUP, release and distribution, architecture and parameter count, I/O modality and format, licence, training process and data, compute, energy, plus extra evaluation and adversarial-testing content for systemic-risk models.

functions.name: Register model artifact
functions.description: Create a new immutable version in the registry of record, bind identifiers, and attach payload pointers.
preconditions: caller is authorized to create versions
registered model exists or may be created
effects: lineage to run recorded if supplied
ingestion time recorded separately from any release time

functions.name: Verify payload integrity
functions.description: Recompute hashes (and signatures if present) and record verifiedUsing results.
preconditions: hash algorithms are in the allowed set
effects: pass or fail recorded with observation time
failed versions must not receive production aliases

functions.name: Emit ML bill of materials
functions.description: Project the artifact to a CycloneDX machine-learning-model component and/or SPDX AIPackage with licence relationships.
inputs: optional dependency graph of libraries and datasets
outputs: CycloneDX ML-BOM and/or SPDX AI document
preconditions: identity, hashes, and licence fields are populated

functions.name: Set deployment alias
functions.description: Point a mutable alias at an immutable version after required checks.
effects: alias now resolves to the target version
previous target loses that alias unless reassigned

functions.name: Attach transparency artifacts
functions.description: Bind model card, evaluation results, and, where applicable, GPAI documentation packs to the version.
preconditions: GPAI packs required if GPAI flag is true and exemption does not apply
effects: card and packs become the current documentation of the version

functions.name: Export interchange format
functions.description: Produce or retrieve an ONNX or other interchange projection with recorded opset and signature.
preconditions: source payload is loadable in a supported library
conversion tools are available or a stored projection exists
effects: projection stored as a payload member or derived artifact

functions.name: Release documentation to authority
functions.description: Package Annex XI technical documentation for the AI Office or national competent authority while preserving confidentiality markings.
preconditions: artifact is a GPAI model subject to Art. 53(1)(a) or an equivalent duty
effects: trade secrets remain marked per Art. 78 handling

functions.name: Retire model version
functions.description: Archive or revoke a version, clear production aliases, and apply retention or deletion rules.
preconditions: production aliases reassigned or explicitly cleared
effects: version no longer served via production aliases
payload deleted or retained per schedule
metadata retained as tombstone if required

composition.purpose: An AI system composes or uses one or more model artifacts; this model stores the used-by link without absorbing system orchestration.
The producing training or fine-tuning run is the provenance source of the artifact.
Evaluation campaigns assess this artifact; attached metrics point at those campaigns.
Declared training, validation, and test datasets remain separate objects.
Align identity, licence relationships, integrity, energy, SPI, and safety fields to the SPDX AI profile without claiming automatic conformance.
Align component type, hashes, PURL, and model-card objects to ML-BOM inventory.

composition.target: ISO/IEC 22989 AI model and machine-learning model
composition.purpose: Use ISO terminology that a model is used in an AI system and is not itself the system.
Align public-hub taxonomy, licence, base_model relations, and eval blocks.
Treat ONNX as an interchange projection of the computational graph, not as a separate governed entity.

owner_package_requirements: Name a natural-person or organizational owner accountable for each registered model family.
Designate one registry of record as the master system for version identifiers.
Require cryptographic hashes of every payload member before any production alias is assigned.
Record declared licence (and concluded licence when SPDX is used) before distribution.
Keep model-card intended-use and limitation text at a fidelity useful to downstream integrators.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint Dimension IRIs under the adopting namespace only after the master-system identifier exists. Prefer SPDX spdxId and Package URL as governed global identifiers; do not mint a new UUID when a registry name-plus-version or PURL already identifies the payload.
registry_links: MLflow Model Registry or equivalent enterprise catalog as master system
Hugging Face Hub model identifiers where the artifact is public
ISO/IEC 22989 terminology register for model versus system

canonicalization_rules: Treat registry name plus immutable version as the canonical business key; hashes confirm payload identity.
Normalize licence identifiers to SPDX licence list ids when they exist; store custom licences as named files with content hashes.
Canonicalize timestamps to RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z.
Treat aliases as mutable indexes, never as identity.
patch_rules: Do not mutate payload bytes of a registered version; register a new version instead.
Patches to metadata (card text, tags, licence conclusions) increment a metadata generation counter and are audit-logged.
Derivation (quantize, adapter merge) always yields a new artifact version with a recorded relation to the base.
compatibility_rules: A new version is compatible for an alias only if the input-output signature is backward compatible or a breaking-change flag is set.
ONNX projections declare opset; consumers must not assume implicit opset upgrades.
SPDX AI profile and CycloneDX ML-BOM are alternative interchange projections; neither is required for internal governance.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier of the model registry of record (registered-model name plus immutable version, or equivalent catalog key)
Governed global identifier or IRI (SPDX AIPackage spdxId, Package URL, CycloneDX purl)
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension when no master-system or global identifier exists
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record all times as RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z. Distinguish event time (training completion, release, hash computation, alias change, retirement) from observation or ingestion time when the Dimension records the artifact later than the event; never treat a date-only value as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Payload files use content-addressed names derived from their hashes; ML-BOM serial numbers use urn:uuid as in CycloneDX; human names remain the registry name and version.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every payload member SHALL have at least one SHA-256 (or stronger) digest recorded before promotion. Prefer Safetensors or ONNX over pickle-based weight formats. Signatures, when present, are additional evidence, not a substitute for hashes.

policies: No production alias without recorded owner, licence, hashes, and intended-use text.
GPAI artifacts placed on the Union market keep Annex XI documentation unless a documented Art. 53(2) exemption applies and systemic risk is absent.
Builders of a version are separated from validators of that version for MEASURE-style independence.
Deleted payloads leave a tombstone metadata record unless law requires full erasure.

read: Any role with artifact-scope grant may read non-confidential metadata.
Payload download requires payload-scope grant or a recorded authority exception.
Annex XI packs are confidential by default.
create: ML engineers may create versions in non-production namespaces.
Registry stewards mint the master-system identifier.
Create is rejected if hashes cannot be computed.
update: Payload bytes are immutable; updates create a new version.
Owners and stewards may update card text, tags, aliases, and licence conclusions with audit.
Validators may write validation_status tags only.
delete: Payload deletion follows the retention schedule and legal-hold check.
Production aliases must be cleared before delete.
Metadata tombstones remain unless a statutory erasure right applies.

roles.name: Model owner
responsibilities: Accountable for intended use, licence, and retirement
Names validators independent of the building team

roles.name: ML engineer
responsibilities: Attaches lineage to the training run

roles.name: Model validator
responsibilities: Assesses the artifact independently of builders
Writes validation_status and attached metrics pointers
Blocks promotion when integrity or evaluation evidence is missing

roles.name: Registry steward
responsibilities: Enforces hash, licence, and alias policies

roles.name: Compliance officer
responsibilities: Maintains copyright policy and training-content summary

roles.name: Downstream integrator
responsibilities: Consumes Annex XII or model-card limitations
Must not treat the artifact as the AI system
Records which system versions load which artifact versions

access.default_rule: Deny payload download and confidential packs; allow metadata read to authenticated roles within the owning package.
exceptions: AI Office or national competent authority requests for Annex XI documentation under Article 53 and Article 78 confidentiality handling
Incident forensics by security roles on hashed payload copies
Open-published artifacts whose licence and AUP permit anonymous download
audit_requirements: Log every alias change, payload download, documentation disclosure, and deletion with actor, event time, and observation time
Retain audit logs at least as long as the metadata tombstone

coverage.claim: This model captures the defensible operating surface of a versioned ML model artifact as an entity distinct from AI systems, training runs, and evaluation campaigns, aligned to ISO terminology, SPDX/CycloneDX inventory, Hugging Face and MLflow identity practice, NIST documentation expectations, and EU GPAI documentation duties. It is not a claim of universal or metaphysical completeness.

checklist.notes: Master-system registry key, SPDX/PURL global identifiers, and Dimension UUID fallback; versions are immutable.
Aliases, status tags, valid-until, retirement, and MLflow stage deprecation are modelled.
Used-by AI system, produced-by training run, evaluated-by campaign, dataset refs, and base/adapter/merge links.
Release, built, valid-until, alias, and ingestion times as RFC 3339 event versus observation times.
Run id, dataset pointers, hyperparameters, hashes, and eval-result sources.
Owner, suppliedBy, manufacturer/authors, and licence as property rights.
Hash verification, validation_status tags, and independent validator role; campaign process remains WM-AI-003.
Default deny on payloads and Annex XI; authority-request exception; audit of downloads.
Retention schedule, legal hold, payload delete versus metadata tombstone.
ONNX projection, SPDX AIPackage, CycloneDX ML-BOM, Hugging Face card schema, PURL.
Safetensors, ONNX, and generic payload members as projections of one entity.
Declared and concluded licences, custom licence files, AUP, GPAI copyright policy.
Attached metrics and thresholds with source; evaluation process out of scope.
SPDX energyConsumption and Annex XI compute/energy fields as artifact documentation.
base_model and relation kinds for fine-tune, adapter, quantized, and merge.
Download location and storage identifier only; no geographic semantics for weights themselves.

known_omissions: Cryptographic model signing and SLSA-style build attestations were not grounded in a fetched primary specification and remain a gap.
Tokenizer, chat-template, and processor files are treated as payload members, not a sibling linguistic-resource model.
Hardware-compiled engines (TensorRT, CoreML) and encrypted or TEE-sealed weights lack primary coverage here.
Continual-learning in-place weight updates conflict with immutable-version rules and need a local policy.
Mixture-of-experts expert-shard identity and federated partial models are not specified.
Full ISO/IEC 22989:2022 clause text was not retrieved; AMD1 generative terms are used from public OBP fragments only.
Model-card Toolkit / Mitchell 2018 academic schema is cited by Hugging Face but was not independently fetched.
conflicts: SPDX AIPackage describes both an AI application and a trained model; this meta-model restricts itself to the trained-model reading and records the conflict.
MLflow still documents stages (Staging/Production/Archived) while recommending aliases; both are modelled, with aliases preferred.
CycloneDX ML-BOM emphasises supply-chain inventory; SPDX AI profile emphasises licence, energy, and safety metadata; alignment is not equivalence.
Hugging Face model-index and newer eval_results formats overlap; either may project into attached metrics.
EU GPAI legal object versus ISO AI-system object: a GPAI model artifact is not automatically an AI system under ISO 22989.
Content-hash identity versus registry version identity diverges if weights are rewritten in place; this model forbids in-place rewrite.
regional_assumptions: EU GPAI Articles 53 and Annex XI/XII apply to models placed on the Union market from 2 August 2025; they do not automatically bind non-EU internal catalogs.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary US public-authority guidance, not a conformity scheme.
Hugging Face Hub identifiers are a de facto public namespace, not a legal registry of record unless so designated by the owner.
SPDX licence identifiers are used as the default licence code system.
adversarial_checks: Would an agent confuse a sharded Safetensors directory with a different logical version if only the first shard is hashed? Mitigated by requiring hashes of every member plus a manifest hash.
Would a LoRA adapter be registered as a patch to the base instead of a new artifact? The model forbids payload mutation and requires a derivation record.
Would open-source GPAI providers drop Annex XI while still needing the public training-content summary and copyright policy? Exemption is modelled as partial.
Would deprecated MLflow stages be treated as identity? Aliases are indexes; stages are optional status.
Would evaluation metrics stored here be mistaken for a completed MEASURE campaign? Questions point to WM-AI-003 for protocols.
Would an ONNX file be governed as a second model rather than a projection? Export function records lineage to the same version.
